prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 2D merge · Clinic schedule (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Time" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Monday" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Tuesday" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Cardiology clinic (Dr. I" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Dermatology" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Staff training — closed " spans 2 col × 1 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Time" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 44px
  col 2: header "Monday › Room A" · longest unbreakable word 74px · one-line width 378px
  col 3: header "Monday › Room B" · longest unbreakable word 87px · one-line width 87px
  col 4: header "Tuesday › Room A" · longest unbreakable word 98px · one-line width 98px
  col 5: header "Tuesday › Room B" · longest unbreakable word 89px · one-line width 367px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A two-day clinic schedule: time rows crossed with Monday/Tuesday and Room A/B columns, showing which clinic is running, when walk-ins are accepted, and when the clinic is closed.","reading":"Readers scan down the Time column for a slot, then across the day/room columns to compare availability. Merged day headers and multi-row clinic cells mean the table is read in blocks rather than cell by cell; the multi-row cells can absorb some prose wrapping before the schedule becomes too tall.","groups":["col 1 (Time) is the row axis and should stay narrow and stable","cols 2–3 form the Monday block, with Room A and Room B as parallel slots under one merged Monday header","cols 4–5 form the Tuesday block, with Room A and Room B as parallel slots under one merged Tuesday header","cols 2 and 5 carry the long clinic prose; cols 3 and 4 are short/empty slots but still carry day/room headers"],"keep_intact":["time labels 09:00, 10:00, 11:00","day names Monday/Tuesday and room labels Room A/Room B where possible","clinic names and identifiers such as Cardiology, Dermatology, Dr. Ito","merged-cell relationships: Monday/Tuesday group their two rooms, and multi-row clinic cells stay associated with their time span"],"may_wrap":["long clinic descriptions such as 'Cardiology clinic (Dr. Ito), walk-ins accepted until 10:30'","the 'Staff training — closed to patients' note","day/room headers may wrap after '›' or between words; avoid splitting words when possible"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [65, 110, 38, 38, 110] · table 362×671px · row heights [36, 129, 176, 176, 153] · column headers wrapped 2/7 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 28 · OVERFLOWS the box by 2px
Design r0B: widths [65, 140, 120, 120, 140] · table 586×286px · row heights [36, 36, 53, 53, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/7 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 226px
Design r0C: widths [65, 399, 108, 119, 388] · table 1080×182px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/7 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 720px
Constraint adjustments applied: r0A: raised a column to the minimum 38px; raised a column to the minimum 38px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
